physicalNotes: No radius or mass of GN-z11 is recorded here: its package frames it at 9,265 pc (object.json worldFrame.bodyRadiusM), half the width of the picture that is drawn at its distance, a presentation value.

sources.position: Oesch et al. (2016), A Remarkably Luminous Galaxy at z = 11.1 Measured with Hubble Space Telescope Grism Spectroscopy, ApJ 819, 129 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00461); text: GN-z11 lies at (RA, DEC) = (12:36:25.46, +62:14:31.4)
sources.distance: Comoving distance of the redshift z = 10.603 (Bunker et al. (2023), JADES NIRSpec Spectroscopy of GN-z11, A&A 677, A88) in the Planck 2018 cosmology: 9762148825.546518 pc, from Astropy 8.0.1 Planck18.comoving_distance (Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209). The project's convention for objects placed by redshift (packages/bake/cli/prepare-catalogue-points.mts).
sources.properMotion: Zero: the object is held at its published position; no motion across the sky is applied.
sources.radialVelocity: c z for the redshift z = 10.603: the redshift written as a velocity, not a motion through space. Bunker et al. (2023), JADES NIRSpec Spectroscopy of GN-z11, A&A 677, A88 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07256); abstract: we derive a redshift of z = 10.603.
